transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2027-01-05
- Time: 10:00 PST
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Hosts: Priya Shah, Lena Ortiz, Marcus Li

Auto-generated Summary:
Priya opened with a quick business update; Lena covered platform resilience and the private deployment roadmap; Marcus ran through capacity and cost levers; Sara talked product priorities and pilot scopes; Evan led an incident retrospective. Q&A included questions on hiring, SOC/ISO timelines, and pricing impact for Dedicated customers.

---
[00:00] Priya: Okay everyone, hey good morning, uh good afternoon depending on where you are. Thanks for jumping in. We've got a compact agenda, aiming for clarity on Q1 and the three cross-team pilots we want to kick off. I'll hand it to Lena for platform highlights.

[00:28] Lena: Thanks Priya. Quick note on uptime we clipped 99.86 last month, there was the customer-facing slip on the 18th which Evan will cover, but the overall trend is better. On private deployments — the VPC onboarding flow — engineering and infra have trimmed the on-boarding time from 7 days to about 3.5 days in the beta. There's still two sticking points: KMS integration and the network egress policy templates. We need the security SME to sign off on the templates.

[01:05] Marcus: Just to add, the Dedicated pool autoscaling now supports burst instances but we saw some cost overshoot in the last microburst because of sizing defaults. We'll be updating the runbook. We're proposing a conservative default that lowers baseline capacity by 12% and adds a ramp window to avoid sudden overprovision.

[01:40] Sara: On product — top level: simplify the pricing tiers and make the Dedicated entry cheaper to experiment with. We'll A/B the new tier with two pilot customers to measure conversion. Pilot targets: 30% lower initial commitment, target P50 latency under 120ms for the 512-token profile.

[02:10] Evan: I'll run the incident retro now — the outage on Dec 18 was a cascading VM reimage triggered by a bad kernel update from a third-party image. TL;DR: our autoscaler misinterpreted a memory pressure signal, created a churn loop, and kv -- sorry K V cache warmup delays made tail latency spike and that triggered more autoscale. We fixed the immediate problem with a hotfix and now plan to add a circuit-breaker to the autoscaler and a grace period for cache warming. I'll post the full timeline later.

[02:55] Attendee 1 (All-Hands chat): was the cert rotation involved?

[03:02] Evan: No cert rotation, that was a separate incident, different day. This was purely kernel image + autoscale rule interaction.

[03:25] Priya: Important commercial note — our churn numbers for midmarket were trending flat; the plan for Q1 is to focus on usage-driven growth and remove friction for Dedicated trials. This ties into the product pilot Sara mentioned. We also need to align on support SLAs for private customers. Marcus?

[03:50] Marcus: SLA conversation: for Dedicated we'll propose a two-tier SLA — standard (99.5) and enterprise (99.9 with more rapid on-call response). That maps to commit and price. The key tradeoff is cost vs latency consistency. We can offer optional pre-warmed pools as an add-on for customers who need consistent p99.

[04:20] Lena: Security/compliance updates: we completed the third SOC2 readiness audit and expect final paperwork mid Q1. ISO27001 is in flight; the auditor visit is scheduled for late Feb. For private customers, the on-prem package will include an audit bundle and an HSM integration doc.

[04:50] Audience question (typed): what about data residency?

[04:58] Priya: Data residency — we have two new regions coming online in EMEA and APAC by end of March. Private deployments can get region-specific storage configs; we'll coordinate legal/regulatory with affected customers.

[05:20] Jordan: Quick org update — hiring plan: we are pacing to add 26 engineers and 8 product/ops folks in Q1. We'll prioritize reliability, infra, and devex. Note: hiring is cautious on comps; many roles will be distributed across EMEA and NA.

[05:45] Sara: On pilot specifics, our three pilots are: 1) Dedicated trial pricing experiment, 2) Private VPC onboarding acceleration with a target of <48 hours, 3) Cost-savings experiment (quantization + batching config suggestions) for high-throughput customers. We want engineering and sales paired on each.

[06:20] Marcus: For pilot #3, quick note: some customers will accept slightly higher latency for 40-60% lower cost. We need to capture acceptable quality deltas via evals. Research will help instrument automatic rollback if quality drops below threshold.

[06:50] Priya: Good point. Research — are we ready to support automated rollback?

[06:58] Lena: We're building eval hooks in the runtime to emit regression signals; not fully automated yet, but the telemetry is there. We need to train the thresholding models and define guardrails.

[07:20] Audience question: any update on model catalog expansion?

[07:29] Sara: We're planning three new curated models next quarter (a multilingual small model, a code-specialized variant, and a compressed 7B variant optimized for GPU TCO). We'll publish performance profiles.

[07:50] Random participant (muffled): can we get better docs on rolling deployments?

[07:55] Marcus: Yes, we'll publish a 'rolling deploys for customers' doc. I'll own that.

[08:10] Priya: All right we'll move to the incident specifics Evan promised.

[08:15] Evan: Timeline bullet points — 03:12 UTC autoscale spike; 03:15 churn started; 03:20 first pager; 03:40 mitigation enacted. Root cause: incorrect memory threshold in the autoscaler combined with a custom kernel image in the infra image set. Action: lock base images and add image gating. We also will add a manual override in the autoscaler UI.

[08:50] Attendee 2: any customer impact?

[08:53] Evan: A small subset of real-time customers saw latency spikes between 3–10 minutes; no data loss, but increased error rates for some streaming sessions. Outreach from CS was performed within 2 hours.

[09:15] Priya: Thank you. Let's talk about cost levers quickly — Marcus?

[09:19] Marcus: We'll push two changes: 1) default batch sizing lowered for low-latency routes; 2) dynamic batching by route type so high-throughput embedding jobs get larger batches. We're targeting a 14% token-cost reduction for 95th percentile workloads.

[09:45] Audience question: how will this affect dev experience?

[09:50] Sara: There will be a dev-ex preview flag. We plan to give teams an opt-in during the pilot and collect feedback.

[10:05] Q&A (rapid fire)
[10:06] Attendee 3: timeline on SSO/SAML for Private?

[10:08] Lena: SSO/SAML will be out in early Feb for private plane — sorry private control plane — we have a couple of PRs waiting for STS integration.

[10:25] Attendee 4: will the billing model change for embeddings?

[10:28] Priya: No immediate changes this quarter, but embeddings pricing will be included in the pilot pricing bundles for Dedicated to drive adoption.

[10:45] Priya: Quick closing recap: three pilots, runbooks and incident writeups due next week, SOC2 finish mid-Q1. We'll post slides and links after the recording. Any last questions?

[11:10] Marcus: One ask — product and sales need to agree on success metrics for the Dedicated experiment by Monday.

[11:30] Sara: I'll set up a 30-minute alignment session with sales and engineering — invite will go out today.

[11:45] Priya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and the tickets from action items. Have a good day.

Post-meeting notes:
- Links shared: runbook draft (internal link), incident timeline (to be published), pilot brief template (will be shared by Sara).
- Tone: pragmatic, a little urgent on reliability and cost.
- Transcription notes: some words mis-transcribed (K V cache vs kv-cache), occasional speaker overlap in Q&A.
